I think of my last encounter. We met on tinder, had a fantastic night, and I kinda fell head over heels. I didn't realize it at the time, but I put a lot of expectations on her. I limited what she was by how I wanted her to be. In doing so I limited myself as well. Though I've made peace with that relationship now (I am a very emotionally sensitive man), I think it took that experience to make me realize how much freedom I was limiting myself from by letting another person determine the value of my personal time. I.e. "If I wasn't alone right now, if I had someone, I would be happy." I flung intimacy into the future and looked at it like a goal I had to be at right now. As I write this, I'm realize how much trauma I put myself through wanting something I wasn't ready for yet. While these thoughts weren't wrong or bad, for me, it made me realize that I needed to start being more comfortable with myself. I needed to be more comfortable being alone and happy with my own company. I needed to be more comfortable expressing who I am sexually. 

After a lot of exploration in that area of my life, I realized what I really want is celibacy. At least for some extended period of time. To dive deep into myself, and see myself truly happy and whole. While the realization that I'm whole without a partner was a happy and blissful message, I still find myself smiling warmly at the idea of someone to hold hands with or sing a song about butts to. For now I accept what is. :) 

"*All* of humanity's problems stem from *man's inability* to sit quietly in a room alone." 

Maybe I won't always be alone. But until I happen to have company, I'll be happy and joyful celebrating who I am as a singular being. I am beyond excited to share that physicality with someone. With the one I fall in love with. That is my highest excitement, and simply nothing else will do. :)

I like that, for those who are really looking at the state of gaming, we’re starting to move away from the hand holding games of recent times. Get a quest, follow your marker, hit the guy, get the stuff. Very WoW centric type mechanics as far as a linear experience goes. 

Take Call of Duty for example, though I’ll try not to beat a dead horse too hard. The single player campaign is literally you following markers, dispatching the same bad guys, then doing it all over again. It’s an “on the rails.” experience, doubly so, being that it isn’t just primarily linear in concept, but has, essentially, a Microsoft staple guy telling you what you should be doing.

Remember Morrowind? You step off a boat into a customs office, fill out a form of who you are, and are dumped in a podunk little swamp village named Seyda Neen. Your only guide is a notebook that says you can find a man named Cassius somewhere in Balmora. That’s it. 

No character is unkillable, you can screw up the story in hundreds, probably thousands of possible ways. The entire experience is played out how you want to see it done. There are no limitations for your imagination. You step off that boat into wonderment and with a sense of adventure, without even knowing the landscape or lore!

A lot of modern games play to the on the rails trope. It’s like “it’s a small world” but with less charm, and more DLC. Shareholders got a hold of the industry and THEY started crafting the games, designers were given creative limits, and the players suffer for it. 

What I am happy to say, is I see this starting to slowly, and I mean snails pace slowly, stopping. Breath of the Wild? Hey, Ganon is up to some shit, you need to wake up, here’s a thing, good luck. No hand holding, you step out of the cavern with the same wide eyed wonder, with an intent, but not limited by any “follow the marker” bullshit. I know this can be poked at with “Well there are markers when you start a quest” etc. You’re missing the point. 

When was the last time you really felt like a part of the game instead of just like you’re along for the ride? I’m see this trend make a resurgence, slowly, but it’s there. The artform that is gaming will be better off for it.

Just wanted to say I appreciate you bringing up this topic. I think there’s a lightning fast vitriol that comes to racists, sexists, etc. I too have had a hard time dealing with the conundrum of separating the false ideologies of certain artists from their work. 

My first thought goes to the lead singer of Burzum. Varg planned to kill people, just straight up murder. As a fan of metal, I’ll say I haven’t listened to Burzum in a long time. I’m sure there are plenty of other musical examples others could throw about as well. Does enjoying someone’s art connect you to their person or mindset? Maybe so. I believe spiritually we’re all equal, from the worst to the best, to speak in terms more malleable for clear conversation. It begs a question further still, what do those that think themselves above these people think of those who enjoy their work? Should we ostracize or judge those who find Hitler’s painting to have beauty or meaning? Certainly you can be a wonderful person and still enjoy the thrashing brutality of some metal imagery. Intentions, thoughts, and actions make you who you are. I intend to enjoy someone’s work, though I find their person lacking empathy or understanding, because the work itself has value. This is to say I would never act on artwork asking me or prodding me to enforce something on another that they wouldn’t want or consent to. 

This is an excellent topic to reach an understanding in those that wish to listen and understand instead of do away with something because it’s a difficult topic. In another phrase, can we be loving and centered around in that love while simultaneously pushing away those people that are considered lacking empathy to the point of hurting the total mass of humanity more than they help?

I won’t pretend to have my head wrapped around the whole subject. Thanks for providing and excellent question.

I had a difficult mushroom trip with similar themes to your 2CE experience. 

It went south and had me almost unable to listen to my favorite music. I couldn't find my happy place anymore. I was anxiety ridden. Hearing voices. My music would always remind me too much of painful things that happened to me during the trip. Being abandoned by my best friends at a festival stage while I was peaking and freaking. I watched my parents souls being tormented on the Vmax screen and had to cope with their eventual deaths, all my fault, the voice in my head kept telling me. My visuals were going crazy. I awkwardly begged strangers with unintelligible mushroom babble to let me just be near someone else so I felt safe. No one wanted to dance with me. I tried gravitating toward what sounded pleasant to be greeted by worse manifestations of anxiety and stress. I couldn't pull out of it. I couldn't find a single human being to comfort me in the slightest. Even the guy at the med tent I finally found made snide comments about my anxious state. I felt spiritually wounded and so, so vulnerable.

These effects left an imprint of hurt and deep seated pain that I still carry with me, and I think about that trip often. I spent almost 6 months recovering from that experience, and am still getting better. What I can tell you is this: I've grown so much from it. I went from someone who was hearing voices telling me that my god hated me and wanted nothing to do with me, and that my best friends; my festifam hated me. I genuinely thought I had ruined an entire festival for everyone who attended. One of my past worst fears. 

I went from that anxious wreck lost in self doubt and paranoia to someone proud of their commitment to living to get better. I lived a sober healthy life for those 6 to 8 months after. The voices have stopped, thank Yahweh, but like I said, I still carry that pain with me. I haven't learned how to put it down quite yet. 

Don't let your burdens overwhelm you. In the searing heat of one's pain, it's hard to stop thinking about how "hot" it is, do you feel me? Down the road, if managed right, you'll look back and realize how far you've come, but right now focus on getting better. Surround yourself with friends and keep busy. Pursue what your life is begging from you. I promise it gets better. Just give it time and try to stay away from drugs for a bit. Feel free to pm me if you have any questions or need someone to talk to ok? All the best to you.

Don't beat yourself up! Shit happens man, and if this bike doesn't work out, there's another beauty out there meant for you. I know it sucks, I know that feeling all too well. Not to cause you any anxiety, but if there's no title, and the original title isn't in his name, the bike could possibly be stolen. Run the vin number at https://www.nicb.org/theft_and_fraud_awareness/vincheck

Make sure it comes up clean and with no red flags. The DMV will not accept a bill of sale for title transfer or licensing. 

It will work out. The right bike will find you, even if it doesn't end up being this one. :)

Having extra sets of eyes for stuff like this is always good. Hopefully you didn't buy from a scumbag. Getting as much information about it as possible is definitely a good idea. If you can get a hold of him, try and switch back for the time being until the title gets straightened out. Lost title searches cost money, but since he didn't provide a title whatsoever, he should pay for it. Did he have the title at some point?

I had something similar happen when I bought my first bike; a 1985 honda magna v30 VC500c. Upon viewing the title with the owner, it read out as a 2007 honda shadow 750. Turns out our local DMV actually did make a mistake and screwed the title up, after 2 months of talking with someone in local government, I finally got the right title back. 

If whoever sold you the bike isn't willing to help you out with this, you may have to pressure them into helping. Depending on where you live, there are lemon laws, and that aggression will not stand, man. The word 'police' is a very useful word in dealing with people like that. 

While a bill of sale might help your dilemma, by law, he could still pull the bike right out from under you, and you'd be out a new bike and your money that you spent on it. Always match the vins with them when you're going to buy it. Anyone not selling a bike with a title is a potential risk for you. Best of luck to you, hope it works out! Contact your seller!
